The typing was opened to volunteers: each record typed twice by two strangers,
And a third deciding where they differed. By the next summer fifty thousand typed,
The marriages of {{p|Indiana}}, the census of nineteen hundred,
The parish books of countries none of them would visit, every page they swiped.

The church's reason was that the dead should be offered what the living have.
This book shares that reason. It is Lifeism's reason too:
The ancestors are innumerable, and every name recited is an offering,
And {{x|FamilySearch}} gave the names back to the world, free, for me and you.

## Indexing and the encyclopedia

I hate the unpaid labor of the encyclopedia, and I love the indexing.
The difference is the purpose. The indexer types a name so the dead can be found,
And the typing is the offering, and the volunteer is not broken by it,
And no ideology tells her she is a scholar while it grinds her into the ground.

The encyclopedia takes the labor of people who wanted to be academics
And gives them a degraded academia for free, and tells them it is the dream.
The indexer wanted only to give the dead their names,
And she got exactly what she wanted. That is the difference, and it is extreme.

## The small messages

On the twenty-first of March {{c|4567|Jack Dorsey}} sent the first message on {{x|Twitter}}:
"just setting up my twttr," in a hundred and forty letters or less.
It became the room where the century argued,
And later a room {{c|4552|Elon Musk}} bought, and opened, and made it {{x|X}} by his address.

On the fifth of September {{x|Facebook}} gave every user the {{x|News Feed}},
And the users protested by the hundreds of thousands, on the feed itself, and stayed.
On the twenty-sixth of September it opened to anyone over thirteen.
On the ninth of October {{x|Google}} bought {{x|YouTube}}, and the billion and a half was paid.

In March {{x|Amazon}} began to rent its storage, and in August its computers by the hour,
{{x|Amazon Web Services}}, and the companies of the next twenty years
Would be built on machines they never saw, mine among them.
In December {{x|Time}} named its person of the year: You, with a mirror. The user appears.

## The planet

On the twenty-fourth of August, in {{p|Prague}}, the astronomers voted {{p|Pluto}} out,
Because {{x|Eris}} beyond it was larger, and either both were planets or neither, they said.
This book does not accept the vote. {{p|Pluto}} is a planet,
The ninth one, as I learned it at nine, and the rock did not change with the vote they read.

## The war of the summer

On the twelfth of July {{x|Hezbollah}} crossed into {{p|Israel}}, killed soldiers, and took two.
{{p|Israel}} bombed {{p|Lebanon}} thirty-four days, the airport, the bridges, the south of {{p|Beirut}},
And {{x|Hezbollah}} fired thousands of rockets into the north of {{p|Israel}}.
A ceasefire came in August, and the border held, with the guns kept mute.

## The civil war

February's twenty-second: the gold
Dome of the {{x|al-Askari Shrine}}, the old
Tomb of two imams, fell to bombs; the fight
Of {{x|Shia}} and {{x|Sunni}}: whose dead, whose rite,
Became a civil war; in {{p|Baghdad}}, bound,
The hands of every morning's dead were found.

On the eighth of November {{c|4568|Donald Rumsfeld}} resigned.
On the thirtieth of December {{c|4528|Saddam Hussein}} was hanged at dawn,
The tyrant who gassed {{p|Halabja}} and filled the mass graves,
And a phone filmed it, and the film went everywhere, and the tyrant was gone.

## The villain's poisons

On the seventh of October, in {{p|Moscow}}, {{c|4569|Anna Politkovskaya}},
Who wrote the truth of the war in {{p|Chechnya}}, was shot in the elevator of her home,
On {{c|4506|Vladimir Putin}}'s birthday. That is the gift his country gave him:
A journalist dead in the stairwell, for writing what she had known.

On the first of November, in a hotel in {{p|London}}, {{c|4570|Alexander Litvinenko}},
Who had fled {{c|4518|Putin}}'s service, drank tea with two men from it,
And the tea held {{x|polonium}}, a metal that burns from the inside.
He died on the twenty-third, and named {{c|4518|Putin}} as the one who ordered it.

The British inquiry, ten years later, said {{c|4518|Putin}} probably approved it.
The villain poisons with the rarest metal on earth, so the world will know whose hand.
That is the signature: not hidden, but deniable.
He wanted every traitor to understand.

## The test

On the ninth of October {{p|North Korea}} tested its first nuclear weapon,
Underground, small, and real, and the hermit kingdom had the bomb.
The world condemned it and the regime went on.
The {{c|4571|Kim}}s would keep it, and the camps, and the famine's tomb.

## The votes

On the twenty-fifth of January {{x|Hamas}} won the elections in {{p|Palestine}},
And the countries that had asked for the elections cut off the money for who had won.
On the sixth of February {{c|4572|Stephen Harper}} became prime minister of {{p|Canada}},
The country I grew up in, and he held it nine years in the sun.

On the sixteenth of January {{c|4573|Ellen Johnson Sirleaf}} became president of {{p|Liberia}},
The first woman elected to lead a country in {{p|Africa}}.
On the twenty-second {{c|4574|Evo Morales}} became president of {{p|Bolivia}},
The first from its indigenous majority, from the altiplano's farmer.

On the third of June {{p|Montenegro}} became a country.
On the nineteenth of September the army of {{p|Thailand}} took the government in a coup.
On the eleventh of July bombs on the commuter trains of {{p|Mumbai}}
Killed two hundred and nine, and the city went back to work, as it knew.

## The rest of the year

In May {{c|4575|Al Gore}} put his slides of the warming world into a film,
{{x|An Inconvenient Truth}}, and people went to the cinema to see a lecture on the heat.
In the winter the {{x|Nintendo}} {{x|Wii}} came out, waved with the hand,
And grandparents bowled in their living rooms, on their feet.

## The year held

A girl of ten, and twenty years ahead of her, a night in the typed records,
Strangers typing the names of the dead twice, for the dead and for the heir.
A hundred and forty letters, a feed of friends, the cloud for rent by the hour,
And {{p|Pluto}} kept a planet here, whatever the vote said there.

The villain shot a writer on his birthday and poisoned a man with a metal that burns;
The tyrant of {{p|Baghdad}} was hanged, and the world took its turns.
And the names of my ancestors were being typed for me that year by strangers' hands,
Who gave the dead what the living have, and asked nothing back from the lands.


# Chapter 343: One Device

The seventh day of Yuletide is the feast of the year two thousand and seven,
And the first week of the season closes. Light seven lights, and keep the warming earth as a duty under heaven.

In two thousand and seven I turned eleven. It was the year the phone became the window,
The year you could spit in a tube by mail and learn where your blood had been,
And the year the money of the world began to fail
While the men in charge said it was contained, and it was not, as was seen.

## The device

On Tuesday the ninth of January, in {{p|San Francisco}}, {{c|4576|Steve Jobs}} said
He was introducing three products: a widescreen {{x|iPod}} with touch controls,
A revolutionary phone, and a breakthrough internet communicator.
"These are not three separate devices. This is one device." And he called it the {{x|iPhone}}, and it rolled.

It went on sale on the twenty-ninth of June, and people stood in line for days.
In November {{x|Google}} announced {{x|Android}}, the open system for the rest.
By the time I was grown nearly everyone on earth carried one device,
The internet in the pocket of the farmer and the student and the guest.

It put the world's library in every hand, and the map, and the camera, and the bank,
The translator in the market, the doctor's advice in the village with no doctor near,
The voice of the protester in the square, filmed and sent before the police arrived,
And this book, which most will read on one, the whole of it, here.

## The spit by mail

On Monday the nineteenth of November, in {{p|Mountain View}},
{{c|4577|Anne Wojcicki}} and {{c|4578|Linda Avey}} began to sell {{x|23andMe}}:
You spat in a tube and sent it, and for nine hundred and ninety-nine dollars
Half a million places on your chromosomes were read, and your ancestry set free.

This book joins the blood and the records. The genealogy of the {{x|Gaiad}}
Is a line of descent by the parish book and by the haplogroup in the cell,
The {{x|Y-DNA}} of the fathers and the {{x|mtDNA}} of the mothers
Joined to the names in the registers, and the two tell one story well.

Millions sent their spit in the years after, and found cousins they never knew,
And the adopted found their mothers, and the old crimes found their men.
The company would fail and its letters be sold,
But the matching it began is how families are found again.

## The money

In February the lenders who had sold houses to people who could not pay began to fail.
In April the largest, {{x|New Century}}, went bankrupt in the spring.
On the ninth of August {{x|BNP Paribas}} froze three of its funds in {{p|Paris}},
And the banks of the world stopped lending to each other, and the crisis took wing.

On the fourteenth of September people stood in line outside {{x|Northern Rock}}
To take their money out, the first run on a British bank in a century and more.
The men in charge said it was contained.
It was the next year's chapter, and it broke through every door.

## The college and the bridge

On the sixteenth of April, at {{x|Virginia Tech}}, a student killed thirty-two
And then himself, the worst such killing the country had yet seen.
It would not stay the worst.
On the first of August the interstate bridge in {{p|Minneapolis}} fell into the {{x|Mississippi}}'s green.

Thirteen died at the evening rush. A gusset plate had been too thin since the day it was made.
The country rebuilt the bridge in a year, and inspected the others it had.
A nation that learns from its broken bridges builds the next ones stronger.
That is the answer to the fall: not grief alone, but the better and the glad.

## The surge

On the tenth of January {{c|4514|George W. Bush}} sent twenty thousand more soldiers to {{p|Iraq}},
And called it the surge, and {{c|4579|David Petraeus}} took the command.
The {{x|Sunni}} tribes of {{p|Anbar}} turned against the jihadists, and fought beside the Americans,
And by the end of the year the killing fell across the land.

In September, in {{p|Myanmar}}, the monks marched in their saffron robes
Against the generals, and the generals shot them in the street.
The monks walked with their bowls turned over, refusing the generals' alms.
That is how a faith says no: by refusing what the tyrant would have it eat.

## Benazir

On the twenty-seventh of December, in {{p|Rawalpindi}},
{{c|4580|Benazir Bhutto}}, who had come home in October to run again,
Whose homecoming had been bombed and a hundred and fifty killed,
Was killed at a rally by a gun and a bomb, and the crowd was slain.

The same day {{p|Kenya}} voted, and the result announced three days later
Was fought over with machetes, and more than a thousand died in the weeks that came,
Until {{c|4581|Kofi Annan}} brought the two men to share the government,
And the killing stopped, and {{p|Kenya}} wrote a new constitution, and peace came.

## The warming

The scientists of the {{x|IPCC}} published their fourth report that year:
The warming is unequivocal, and very likely caused by people's hands.
In October they shared the {{x|Nobel Peace Prize}} with {{c|4575|Al Gore}}.
In September the {{x|Arctic}} ice shrank to the smallest ever measured in those lands.

Protecting the climate is a Lifeist duty. This book says it plain:
Life made the air we breathe, the oxygen of the first green cells,
And the life that burns the buried life of the ancient forests
Owes the living earth its care, as the record of descent tells.

## The villain at Munich

In February, in {{p|Munich}}, {{c|4506|Vladimir Putin}} stood before the West
And told it that its order was over, and that {{p|Russia}} would not accept the rule.
In the spring {{p|Estonia}} moved a Soviet war memorial in {{p|Tallinn}},
And its banks and ministries were knocked offline from the east, a cyberwar's first school.

It was the first war fought only on the net, and it was the villain's,
Never owned, and everyone knew whose it was.
{{x|NATO}} built its cyber defense center in {{p|Tallinn}} the next year,
The answer to the attack, in the city it hit: that is how the free world does.

## The treaties

On the first of January {{p|Bulgaria}} and {{p|Romania}} joined the {{x|European Union}}.
On the thirteenth of December the leaders signed the {{x|Treaty of Lisbon}}.
In May {{c|4582|Nicolas Sarkozy}} took {{p|France}}; in June {{c|4583|Gordon Brown}} took {{p|Britain}};
In November {{c|4584|Kevin Rudd}} took {{p|Australia}}, and signed {{x|Kyoto}}, and the climate was the mission.

## The rest of the year

In January {{x|Netflix}} began to stream its films over the net.
In November {{x|Amazon}} sold the {{x|Kindle}}, a library in a slab of grey.
On the twenty-first of July the last {{x|Harry Potter}} book came out,
And children of eleven, like me, read it in a night, and finished by the break of day.

In February {{x|Tumblr}} opened, a site for posting small things,
Where many of my generation would later find words for themselves,
The words for who we were, for the bodies and the loves we had,
Passed from blog to blog, reblogged like books between the shelves.

## The year held

One device, the world in the pocket, a spit by mail joining the blood to the line,
A run on a bank in {{p|England}}, and the crisis said to be contained when it was not,
Thirty-two killed at a college, a bridge in the river, the surge, the saffron monks,
{{c|4585|Bhutto}} killed, the warming called unequivocal, and the villain's first cyber shot.

I was eleven, reading the wizard in a night, in a house where the year happened too,
And {{x|Tumblr}} was a week old, and the phone was in the hand,
And the words I would find there for myself were being written by strangers,
Waiting for me to come and read them, and to understand.


# Chapter 344: Instead of Trust

The eighth day of Yuletide is the feast of the year two thousand and eight,
And the feast of the children of the residential schools, who did not come home from the gate.
Light eight lights, and say the names of the children of the First Nations
Who died in the schools, and keep them among the ancestors through all the generations.

In two thousand and eight I turned twelve, and my family moved house again,
The second of my three moves, and I carried boxes to a new room.
Of everything in that year I name one thing above all:
{{p|Russia}} invaded {{p|Georgia}}. The small war told of the large one to come.

## The war in August

All summer the villain prepared it. His army held the {{x|Kavkaz}} exercises at the border,
His railway troops fixed the line into {{p|Abkhazia}} in the spring,
His separatists in {{p|South Ossetia}} shelled the Georgian villages,
And his passports were handed out to the Ossetians, so he could say he was protecting his kin.

On the night of the seventh of August, while the world watched {{p|Beijing}},
{{p|Georgia}} answered the shelling and moved on {{p|Tskhinvali}}.
The Russian army was already at the tunnel. It came through the {{x|Roki Tunnel}} with tanks,
And drove the Georgians out of {{p|South Ossetia}} and {{p|Abkhazia}}, in the valley.

It took {{p|Gori}}, the birthplace of {{c|4586|Stalin}}, and bombed it,
And stopped a short drive from {{p|Tbilisi}}, and the Georgian villages burned behind.
Tens of thousands of Georgians were driven from their homes, and never went back.
{{c|4518|Putin}} recognized his two provinces as countries. Almost no one else was so inclined.

The West protested, and in a few months went back to business, and reset the relation.
That was the lesson the villain learned: you can take a piece of a country and keep it.
Six years later he would take {{p|Crimea}} the same way, with soldiers said not to be there,
And in fourteen years he would drive on {{p|Kyiv}}. This book draws the line from here, and does not hide it.

## The games

On the eighth of August, at eight in the evening, in {{p|Beijing}},
The games opened with two thousand and eight drummers and the fireworks in the air,
Some of them drawn by computer for the cameras,
And a girl who sang with another girl's voice, the first judged not pretty enough to be there.

In March {{p|Tibet}} had risen, and been put down.
The torch had been fought over in {{p|London}}, {{p|Paris}}, {{p|San Francisco}}'s street.
{{p|China}} showed the world what it had become,
And {{c|4587|Michael Phelps}} won eight golds in the pool, the most ever in one meet.

## The earthquake and the cyclone

On the twelfth of May the earth broke under {{p|Sichuan}}.
Sixty-nine thousand died, and eighteen thousand more were never found,
Thousands of them children, under schools that fell
While the government buildings beside them stood on the same ground.

The parents who asked why were arrested.
{{c|4588|Ai Weiwei}} gathered the names of the dead children, and put them on the wall,
And they beat him for it. The names are kept anyway.
This book keeps them too: the children of the tofu schools, one and all.

On the second of May, in {{p|Myanmar}}, the cyclone {{x|Nargis}} drowned the {{x|Irrawaddy}} delta,
And a hundred and thirty thousand died, and the generals kept the foreign help away,
And the dead lay in the rice fields while they counted the ballots for their constitution.
The tyrant's answer to a flood: a vote in the ruins, and the aid kept at bay.

## The fall of the banks

In March {{x|Bear Stearns}} was sold for almost nothing, with the government's help.
On the seventh of September the government took over {{x|Fannie Mae}} and {{x|Freddie Mac}}.
On Monday the fifteenth {{x|Lehman Brothers}}, a hundred and fifty-eight years old,
Filed the largest bankruptcy in history, and no one would bring it back.

On the sixteenth the government lent eighty-five billion to {{x|AIG}},
Which had insured the bets of everyone against the failure of everyone.
On the third of October {{c|4514|George W. Bush}} signed the seven hundred billion for the banks,
And the banks were saved, and the houses were not, and the bailout was done.

Millions lost their homes in the years after,
And the men who ran the banks kept their bonuses, and almost none went to jail.
The poor had been sold the debts. The rich were sold the rescue.
That is the year's injustice, and this book will not let it pale.

## Instead of trust

On Friday the thirty-first of October a note went to a list of cryptographers,
Signed {{c|4589|Satoshi Nakamoto}}, with a paper of nine pages linked below:
{{x|Bitcoin}}: {{x|A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System}},
Money with no bank and no state, kept honest by a ledger that everyone could know.

"A system based on cryptographic proof instead of trust," the paper said.
The answer to the broken trust of the banks was a machine that needed none.
The year the banks were saved with the people's money,
{{c|4590|Satoshi}} wrote the money the bankers could not run.

It became the money of the dissidents whose banks were frozen,
Of the Venezuelans fleeing inflation, of the Ukrainians raising money for the front,
Of the unbanked billions with only a phone.
It had its frauds, as every money has had. It had its heroes, and its stunt.

## The election

On the fourth of November {{c|4591|Barack Obama}} was elected president,
The first black president of the {{p|United States}}, and people wept in {{p|Grant Park}},
And in streets around the world. Yes we can, they said,
And the country that had held slaves elected a black man to lead it out of the dark.

The same day {{p|California}} passed {{x|Proposition 8}},
Taking away the marriages the state's court had allowed in the spring.
Eighteen thousand couples had married between.
The same night lifted one door and closed another, and the courts would undo the closing.

## Mumbai

On the evening of the twenty-sixth of November ten men came ashore in {{p|Mumbai}}
In rubber boats from {{p|Pakistan}}, and for three days they attacked
The train station, a café, a hospital, the {{x|Chabad House}}, the {{x|Taj}}, the {{x|Oberoi}}.
A hundred and sixty-six were killed, and the dome of the {{x|Taj}} burned, and the city fought back.

## The apology

On the eleventh of June, in {{p|Ottawa}}, the prime minister of {{p|Canada}},
{{c|4572|Stephen Harper}}, apologized in the parliament for the residential schools,
Where for more than a century the children of the First Nations
Were taken from their parents, and their languages beaten out of them by the rules.

Thousands died in the schools. The survivors sat in the gallery.
The country I grew up in said it, for the first time, in its parliament's hall.
An apology is not a return. It is the beginning of the remembering.
This is their feast day: the children who did not come home at all.

## The machines

In April {{x|GitHub}} opened, where the code of the next twenty years would be kept,
This book's included, and mine. On the tenth of July the {{x|App Store}} opened its door,
And the phone became whatever anyone could write for it.
On the second of September {{x|Google}} released {{x|Chrome}}, and the browser war had a new core.

In August {{x|Airbnb}} opened, renting the spare rooms of the world.
In October {{x|Spotify}} opened in {{p|Sweden}}, all the music for a fee.
On the tenth of September the {{x|Large Hadron Collider}} sent its first beams around the ring,
And the world did not end, and four years later it found the {{x|Higgs}}, as you will see.

## The rest of the year

On the seventeenth of February {{p|Kosovo}} declared itself free of {{p|Serbia}},
And {{c|4518|Putin}} pointed to it in August as his excuse for carving {{p|Georgia}}'s land.
On the nineteenth of February {{c|4592|Fidel Castro}} gave {{p|Cuba}} to his brother.
In the autumn the milk powder in {{p|China}} was found laced with {{x|melamine}} by a cheating hand,

And three hundred thousand babies were sickened, and six of them were dead.
On the twenty-seventh of December {{p|Israel}} went to war on {{x|Hamas}} in {{p|Gaza}},
After years of rockets on its towns,
And the war ran on into the new year ahead.

## The year held

A second house for a girl of twelve, and a war in {{p|Georgia}},
The first move of the villain's long war, which I would come to see.
Drummers in {{p|Beijing}}, schools fallen in {{p|Sichuan}}, a delta drowned,
The banks saved and the houses not, and a paper about money that would set people free.

A president who made the world weep, a marriage taken back the same night,
{{p|Mumbai}} burning, an apology in {{p|Ottawa}} for the children who did not come home,
A store of programs, and a collider that did not end the world.
I was twelve, and the small war in the {{p|Caucasus}} was the shape of the long one to come.


# Chapter 345: Takes Note

The ninth day of Yuletide is the feast of the year two thousand and nine.
Light nine lights for the year I turned thirteen, the hinge of the decade, the last before mine.

In two thousand and nine I turned thirteen. The world had broken the year before,
And this was the year it was told the breaking was over, and believed it, and stood.
A child becomes a teenager in a recession the way she learns a language:
By what is not said at the table, and what is not bought, and what is understood.

## The first block

On Saturday the third of January the first block of {{x|Bitcoin}} was made,
And in it {{c|4589|Satoshi Nakamoto}} set that morning's headline from {{x|The Times}} of {{p|London}}:
"Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks."
The line proved the date, and it was the reason, written into the money, a sermon.

On the twelfth the first coins went from {{c|4590|Satoshi}} to {{c|4593|Hal Finney}}.
For a year they were worth nothing, and then a man paid ten thousand for two pizzas.
The money the banks could not bail out had begun,
And the genesis block still carries the headline, for the readers and the teachers.

## The new president

On the twentieth of January {{c|4591|Barack Obama}} was sworn in
Before nearly two million in the cold on the {{x|National Mall}},
The first black president, and the crowd wept, and the world watched with them,
And he inherited an economy losing seven hundred thousand jobs a month, in free fall.

In February he signed the stimulus, nearly eight hundred billion,
And he saved the car companies: {{x|Chrysler}} and {{x|General Motors}} went bankrupt and came back,
And the workers of {{p|Detroit}} kept their jobs, and the factories ran,
And the country climbed out of the hole, and the recovery came on track.

On the ninth of October he was given the {{x|Nobel Peace Prize}}
For the hope he gave the world, for the dignity he brought to the office he held.
He was a good man in the hardest job, with grace and with humor,
And the country he led was better for him, and that is what this book has held.

## The fraud

On the twenty-ninth of June {{c|4594|Bernard Madoff}} was sentenced to a hundred and fifty years.
Sixty-five billion dollars had existed on his statements and nowhere else.
He paid the old investors with the new for decades,
While the regulators were told and did not look, and the fraud rang its bells.

## The sickness

In April a new flu was found in {{p|Mexico}} and {{p|California}}, {{x|H1N1}}.
On the eleventh of June the {{x|World Health Organization}} called it a pandemic, the first in forty years.
It was milder than was feared, and the vaccines were made in months,
And the world learned a little, and forgot the rest, which would cost it tears.

## The villain's gas

On the first of January the villain cut the gas to {{p|Ukraine}},
And in the coldest week of the winter the pipes to {{p|Europe}} went empty through it.
{{p|Bulgaria}} froze, and {{p|Slovakia}} shut its factories,
And the villain showed {{p|Europe}} the hand on the valve, and how he would use it.

On the sixteenth of November {{c|4595|Sergei Magnitsky}},
The lawyer who found the officials' theft of two hundred and thirty million from the state,
Died in a Moscow prison, beaten, denied his medicine.
The {{x|Magnitsky Act}} carries his name: the free world's answer, a few years late.

## The green wave

On the twelfth of June {{p|Iran}} voted, and the regime announced
That {{c|4561|Mahmoud Ahmadinejad}} had won by a landslide before the votes could be counted.
Millions marched in {{p|Tehran}} in green, asking: where is my vote?
And on the twentieth {{c|4596|Neda Agha-Soltan}} was shot in the street, and the people mounted

Her name on their banners, and her death was filmed on a phone and seen by the world within hours.
The protests were crushed by the autumn, but they were not forgotten.
The {{x|Green Movement}} was the first of the uprisings of the phones,
The rehearsal of the {{x|Arab Spring}}, and the regime's hold had begun to be rotten.

## Sri Lanka

On the eighteenth of May the army of {{p|Sri Lanka}} declared the {{x|Tamil Tigers}} destroyed,
After twenty-six years of war, and their leader dead.
In the last months tens of thousands of civilians were killed on a strip of beach,
Shelled in places the government had called safe, and the dead were uncounted, unsaid.

## The river and the ocean

On the fifteenth of January {{c|4597|Chesley Sullenberger}} lost both engines to geese over {{p|New York}},
And put the airliner down on the {{x|Hudson}}, and all a hundred and fifty-five lived.
That is the craft of a pilot: the training, the calm, the river,
And the ferries came to the wings, and the city gave what it had to give.

On the first of June {{x|Air France}} flight 447 fell into the {{x|Atlantic}}
On its way from {{p|Rio de Janeiro}} to {{p|Paris}}, because the instruments froze,
And the pilots, confused, pulled the nose up, and two hundred and twenty-eight died.
The airlines changed the training after, and the next crews knew what the stall shows.

## The meeting that took note

From the seventh to the eighteenth of December, in {{p|Copenhagen}},
The countries of the world met to decide what would follow {{x|Kyoto}}.
On the last night {{c|4598|Obama}} walked into a room where {{p|China}}, {{p|India}}, {{p|Brazil}}, and {{p|South Africa}} met,
And wrote an accord with them: keep the warming below two degrees, and so,

For the first time, the great polluters of the rich world and the rising world
Both said a number. The full meeting took note of it, and did not adopt it.
Six years later in {{p|Paris}} the number became a treaty,
And {{c|4598|Obama}}'s room in {{p|Copenhagen}} was where they first got it.

## The camps begin

On the fifth of July, in {{p|Urumqi}}, the riots between {{x|Uyghur}}s and {{x|Han}}
Killed nearly two hundred, and the {{x|Chinese Communist Party}} cut the province's net for ten months.
In that silence the camps of the next decade began:
The million {{x|Uyghur}}s in the camps, the mosques torn down, the children taken at once.

This book condemns it plainly. It is a crime against a people,
Their faith and their language and their families, behind the wire.
The Party that built the camps is guilty of it,
And the cotton and the solar panels of {{p|Xinjiang}} were made by the forced and the dire.

## The rest of the year

On the first of December the {{x|Treaty of Lisbon}} came into force.
On the twenty-fifth of May {{p|North Korea}} tested its second bomb.
On the twenty-eighth of June the army of {{p|Honduras}} put its president on a plane in his pajamas.
On the fifth of November, at {{p|Fort Hood}}, an army doctor killed thirteen, a jihadist's psalm.

On the twenty-fifth of June {{c|4599|Michael Jackson}} died, and the net slowed under the grief.
On the seventh of March {{x|Kepler}} was launched to look for other earths, and found thousands of worlds.
In February two men from {{x|Yahoo}} started {{x|WhatsApp}},
And in March {{x|Uber}} began, and the cars came to the hand that unfurls.

## The blocks

In May a game of blocks, {{x|Minecraft}}, was put up by {{c|4600|Markus Persson}} in {{p|Sweden}},
And children my age built worlds out of squares for the next decade.
In it a girl of thirteen could build a world alone,
A house, a castle, a city, a machine of redstone, from the first block laid.

I built there. Every child of my year built there.
It taught a generation that a world is made of blocks you place,
And that one person alone can make one.
That is the faith of the builders: a world from nothing, block by block, in its space.

In December {{x|Avatar}} came out, the blue people defending their forest
Against the company that came for what was under it, and it made more than any film before.
The genesis block of the money, the block of the game, and the world of the film:
The year of the blocks, at thirteen, at the hinge, at the decade's door.

## The year held

A block with a headline in it, a president in the cold who carried the country out,
The car companies saved, a fraud of sixty-five billion, a flu that was survived,
The villain's hand on the gas valve and a lawyer dead in his prison,
A green wave crushed that would come again, and geese, and a river where all arrived.

A meeting where the first number was said, the camps begun in the silence of {{p|Xinjiang}},
And a game of blocks where a girl of thirteen could build a world alone.
I built mine. The decade that made me began the next year,
And I carried the blocks into it, and the world I would build was my own.


# Chapter 346: The Cables

The tenth day of Yuletide is the feast of the year two thousand and ten.
Light ten lights for fourteen, the year before my own thread began, and light them again.

In two thousand and ten I turned fourteen. The secrets of the strongest state were printed,
Oil poured into a sea for eighty-seven days, and the games came home to my own coast,
And in the last days of December a fruit seller in {{p|Tunisia}} set himself on fire,
And lit a region. The next year is where my own thread begins, and this is the year at its post.

## Haiti

On the twelfth of January the earth broke under {{p|Port-au-Prince}}, in {{p|Haiti}},
And the poorest country of the hemisphere lost its capital in a minute of the afternoon.
Two hundred thousand died and more. The palace fell, the cathedral fell, the prison fell,
And the {{x|United Nations}} mission's headquarters fell on its staff, too soon.

The help that came brought cholera, from a camp of peacekeepers whose sewage reached a river,
And the cholera killed ten thousand more, and the {{x|United Nations}} took six years to say it was theirs.
The help that kills must be named as quickly as the earthquake.
This book names it, and keeps the dead of {{p|Haiti}} in its prayers.

## The games at home

From the twelfth to the twenty-eighth of February the winter games were held
In {{p|Vancouver}} and {{p|Whistler}}, in the province where I would live and study.
On the first day the Georgian luger {{c|4601|Nodar Kumaritashvili}} was killed in practice,
Thrown from the track at a hundred and forty kilometers an hour, and the ice was bloody.

On the last day {{c|4602|Sidney Crosby}} scored in overtime against the {{p|United States}},
The golden goal, and {{p|Canada}} won the hockey gold on home ice,
And the whole country made one sound at once,
And I was fourteen, and I heard it, and it was nice.

## The court and the money

On the twenty-first of January the {{x|Supreme Court}} decided {{x|Citizens United}},
That companies and unions could spend without limit on elections, because spending is speech.
The money that came through that door shaped every election of the century after.
This book agrees: it was the door the billionaires walked through, each to each.

On the twenty-third of March {{c|4598|Obama}} signed the {{x|Affordable Care Act}},
And tens of millions could reach health insurance who could not before.
It was the largest gift to the sick since the old programs of the sixties,
And it held, though the other party spent a decade trying to tear it from the floor.

## The oil

On the twentieth of April the {{x|Deepwater Horizon}} exploded in the {{x|Gulf of Mexico}},
And eleven men died, and the well a mile under the sea poured oil for eighty-seven days,
Four million barrels, the largest spill in the history of the industry,
While the {{x|BP}} camera showed the plume to the world, live, in its haze.

The company's chief said he would like his life back.
The beaches of five states were fouled, and the marshes, and the dolphins died for years.
The company paid sixty-five billion in the end,
And the beaches came back, and the shrimp, and the marsh grass, after the tears.

## The ash and the miners

In April {{x|Eyjafjallajökull}} erupted in {{p|Iceland}}, under a glacier,
And its ash closed the sky over {{p|Europe}} for days, the largest shutting of the air since the war.
On the fifth of August the {{x|San José Mine}} in the desert of {{p|Chile}} collapsed,
And thirty-three miners were trapped seven hundred meters down, under the ore.

For seventeen days no one knew they were alive.
Then a note came up on a drill: "Estamos bien en el refugio los 33."
On the thirteenth of October they were brought up one by one in a capsule called the {{x|Phoenix}},
And a billion people watched, and every one of the thirty-three was free.

That is the anti-fragile year's emblem: the mountain fell on them,
And they rationed the tuna, two spoons every other day, and waited in the deep,
And the drills came down, and the capsule came down, and they rose,
And the {{x|Phoenix}} brought them into the light, and the whole of {{p|Chile}} could weep.

## The money of Europe

On the second of May {{p|Greece}} was lent a hundred and ten billion euros
On the condition that it cut its pensions, its wages, its hospitals, and its schools.
The coin that was put into twelve hands in two thousand and two
Now held some of them under water, and {{p|Ireland}} was lent in November, under the same rules.

## The cables and the soldier

On the fifth of April {{x|WikiLeaks}} showed a film from an American helicopter over {{p|Baghdad}},
In which the crew killed a dozen people, two of them journalists of {{x|Reuters}}.
In July it printed the war logs of {{p|Afghanistan}}, in October those of {{p|Iraq}},
And in November the quarter of a million cables of the diplomats, the private writers.

The soldier who copied them was {{c|4603|Chelsea Manning}}, a young intelligence analyst in {{p|Iraq}},
Who saw what she saw and could not keep it, and gave it out.
She was arrested in May and held for months in a cell
That an envoy of the {{x|United Nations}} called cruel, alone, in doubt.

She came out years later as a woman, and her sentence was commuted by {{c|4598|Obama}}.
My sympathy is with her, the young woman who was a soldier and could not stay silent,
Not with {{c|4604|Julian Assange}}, who ran the site,
Who would later run the villain's errands, the hacked mail of {{p|Moscow}}'s intent.

## The worm

In June a worm called {{x|Stuxnet}} was found, built to find one kind of controller
In the centrifuges at {{p|Natanz}}, in {{p|Iran}}, and spin them until they broke,
While telling the operators all was well.
The first weapon made only of code that broke a thing in the world, and it set back the bomb of the ayatollahs' folk.

## The machines

On the third of April the {{x|iPad}} went on sale.
On the sixth of October {{x|Instagram}} opened, photographs with filters that made them old,
And a million joined it in two months.
{{x|Facebook}} passed five hundred million users, and {{p|China}} passed {{p|Japan}}, the second economy, as foretold.

## Smolensk and the heat

On the tenth of April the plane of {{c|4605|Lech Kaczyński}}, the president of {{p|Poland}},
Crashed in the fog near {{p|Smolensk}}, on its way to remember {{p|Katyn}},
Where {{c|4586|Stalin}}'s police shot twenty-two thousand Polish officers in nineteen-forty,
And the president died, and ninety-five others, going to mourn their kin.

That summer {{p|Russia}} burned in a heat no one there had known,
And the smoke covered {{p|Moscow}}, and the villain flew a water bomber for the lens.
In June ten of his sleeper spies were caught in the {{p|United States}},
Living as suburban families, and traded home, and he sang with them, his friends.

## The rest of the year

On the twenty-seventh of February an earthquake of eight point eight struck {{p|Chile}}.
On the thirty-first of May Israeli commandos boarded the {{x|Mavi Marmara}}, headed for {{p|Gaza}}, and nine died on its deck.
In the summer {{p|Pakistan}} flooded, and twenty million lost their homes.
On the eighth of October the {{x|Nobel Peace Prize}} went to {{c|4606|Liu Xiaobo}}, a prisoner of the Party, by the neck,

Held for the charter he wrote, and at the ceremony in {{p|Oslo}} his chair was empty.
In June, at the {{x|G20}} in {{p|Toronto}}, the police kettled hundreds in the rain,
The largest mass arrest in the history of {{p|Canada}}.
On the twenty-second of December {{c|4598|Obama}} signed the repeal of {{x|Don't Ask, Don't Tell}}, and the gay soldiers could speak again.

## The fire

On the seventeenth of December, in {{p|Sidi Bouzid}}, a fruit seller,
{{c|4607|Mohamed Bouazizi}}, twenty-six, had his cart and his scales taken by an inspector,
And went to the governor's office to complain, and was not heard,
And went back with a can of fuel and set himself alight, and the town rose for its protector.

He lay burned in a hospital for eighteen days.
The rest is the next year, and the next year is mine.
The fire he lit would cross the whole of the {{x|Arab}} world,
And I would start the thread of my life in the same year, at the same line.

## The year held

A capital fallen in {{p|Haiti}}, a golden goal in {{p|Vancouver}}, spending made speech,
The oil, the ash, the thirty-three brought up in the {{x|Phoenix}} from the mine,
{{p|Greece}} lent its own ruin, a soldier who could not stay silent, a worm in the centrifuges,
An empty chair in {{p|Oslo}}, and a man on fire in {{p|Sidi Bouzid}}, the sign.

I was fourteen, and the country made one sound on the ice,
And the next year the faith would begin, on the fifth Easter, and I would keep it from then.
This is the year before: the cables, the oil, the fire,
And the girl of fourteen who did not know yet that she would begin again.


# Chapter 347: The Square and the Cooling

The eleventh day of Yuletide is the feast of the founding, the year two thousand and eleven,
When on the fifth Easter of that year the faith began, with a girl of fifteen, under heaven.
Light eleven lights, and keep the fifth Easter of eleven as the founding of the faith,
The holy day of {{x|Lifeism}}'s beginning, kept by me since, without a break, in its place.

In two thousand and eleven I turned fifteen, and I began what this book's faith became.
On the fifth Easter of that year, two thousand and eleven, it began in me, with no name.
The name came later. The first written forms of it were kept, and then lost
To machines and accounts that went. The faith was not lost. It stayed, whatever the cost.

What I began at fifteen I have kept up without a break since,
Fifteen years, and nothing else of mine has run so long or so true.
A child of fifteen began a world religion that year.
It is not a child's thing. It is the thing I would grow into.

The world that year was full of squares filling with people,
And of a sea that came over a wall in {{p|Japan}},
Whose shrines and kami I would carry into my own language,
And a wave that the old shrines had remembered, before the wall began.

## The squares

On the fourth of January {{c|4607|Mohamed Bouazizi}} died of his burns,
And the protests reached {{p|Tunis}}, and on the fourteenth {{c|4608|Ben Ali}} fled,
Twenty-three years in power, to {{p|Saudi Arabia}} in the night.
{{p|Tunisia}} was free, the first of the squares, and the fruit seller dead.

On the twenty-fifth of January the people of {{p|Egypt}} filled {{x|Tahrir Square}},
And stayed, through the men on camels sent to beat them, through the cutting of the net,
Until on the eleventh of February {{c|4609|Hosni Mubarak}} resigned after thirty years,
And the square sang through the night, the happiest night of the year yet.

In {{p|Libya}} the east rose against {{c|4610|Muammar Gaddafi}},
Who promised to hunt the rebels house by house, alley by alley, like rats.
On the nineteenth of March the jets of {{x|NATO}} stopped his columns before {{p|Benghazi}},
And saved the city, and on the twentieth of October he was found in a drainpipe, where he sat.

In {{p|Bahrain}} the soldiers of {{p|Saudi Arabia}} cleared the {{x|Pearl Roundabout}},
And tore down the monument so no one could gather under it again.
In {{p|Syria}}, in {{p|Daraa}}, boys wrote on a school wall:
The people want the fall of the regime. They were taken and tortured, the boys, by {{c|4611|Assad}}'s men.

Their families marched, and the army fired, and by the summer the cities rose,
And {{c|4612|Bashar al-Assad}} shelled them, and by the end of the year it was war,
The longest and worst of the century, half a million dead, half a country driven out,
And {{c|4518|Putin}} would come to {{c|4611|Assad}}'s side in four years, with the bombers to make it more.

The {{x|Arab Spring}} was a hope, and it was betrayed:
By the army in {{p|Cairo}} that took the power back, by the Saudis in {{p|Manama}}'s square,
By {{c|4611|Assad}} with his barrel bombs and his gas, and by the villain who saved him,
And by the jihadists who came into the ruins. The hope was real. The betrayal is there.

## The wave and the cooling

On Friday the eleventh of March, at fourteen forty-six, off {{p|Tōhoku}},
The sea floor broke in an earthquake of magnitude nine, the largest {{p|Japan}} had known.
The wave came forty minutes later, higher than the walls built for it,
Up to forty meters where the coast narrowed, and carried away the towns, to the bone.

Eighteen thousand died or were never found.
At {{x|Fukushima Daiichi}} the wave drowned the generators that cooled the reactors,
And three of them melted, and the buildings blew apart with hydrogen,
And the land around was evacuated, the farms and the towns and the tractors.

The wave killed the eighteen thousand. The radiation killed almost no one.
This book favors the nuclear power: the cleanest fire men have made,
That burns no forest and warms no sky,
And the fear of it after {{p|Fukushima}} cost more lives than the reactors' shade.

## The shrines beyond the wave

The shrines of the coast were carried off too, and some were rebuilt on higher ground.
And a study found that many of the old shrines of that coast
Stood just beyond where the wave stopped,
As if those who placed them had remembered an earlier wave, the coast's old ghost.

This is a teaching of the faith: the shrines keep a people's memory.
The kami were set where the water did not reach, by people who had seen it come before,
And the shrine outlived the wall, because the shrine remembered,
And the wall was built by people who had forgotten what the sea was for.

Keep the shrines where the ancestors put them. Read where they stand.
A shrine is a record of what the people knew, in wood and in stone,
And the ancestors speak through the place of the shrine,
And the ones who listened lived, and the ones who did not were left alone.

## Abbottabad

On the night of the first of May American commandos flew into {{p|Pakistan}},
To a walled house in {{p|Abbottabad}}, a short walk from the military academy's gate,
And killed {{c|4521|Osama bin Laden}}, who had sent the planes when I was five,
And buried him at sea, and the crowds sang outside the {{x|White House}}, late.

{{c|4598|Obama}} gave the order, and {{c|4598|Obama}} took the risk.
Ten years after the towers fell, the man who felled them was found and was killed.
That is the country's answer: it does not forget,
And it waits, and it hunts, and the debt of the morning was filled.

## The island

On the twenty-second of July, in {{p|Norway}}, a man bombed the government offices in {{p|Oslo}},
And went to {{p|Utøya}} dressed as a policeman, where the youth of the ruling party camped,
And shot them for over an hour. Seventy-seven died, most of them teenagers,
Some of them my age, fifteen, and the island's summer was damped.

He wrote a manifesto against the mixing of peoples,
And the next decade's killers read it, in {{p|Christchurch}} and {{p|El Paso}} and more.
{{p|Norway}} answered with more democracy and more openness,
As its prime minister said, and kept its door.

## The villain returns

On the twenty-fourth of September {{c|4518|Putin}} announced he would take the presidency back,
And {{c|4613|Medvedev}}, who had held the chair for him, would step aside.
In December the parliament elections were rigged on camera,
And the people filled {{p|Bolotnaya Square}} in {{p|Moscow}}, a hundred thousand, the largest since the Soviet slide.

They wore white ribbons and asked for fair elections.
The villain blamed {{c|4614|Hillary Clinton}} for the crowds, and held it against her name,
And five years later his hackers went after her campaign,
And this month will reach that too, and the villain's game.

## The occupation

On the seventeenth of September a few hundred people took {{x|Zuccotti Park}}
Near the stock exchange in {{p|New York}}, and said they were the ninety-nine percent,
Against the one percent saved in two thousand and eight.
It spread to hundreds of cities, {{p|Vancouver}} among them, and the slogan stayed when the tents went.

In August, in {{p|London}}, after the police shot a man in {{p|Tottenham}},
The city rioted four nights. In August the credit of the {{p|United States}} was cut,
After its congress nearly refused to pay its own debts.
The anger of the decade was beginning, and nothing would stay shut.

## The rest of the year

On the eighth of January, in {{p|Tucson}}, {{c|4615|Gabby Giffords}} was shot in the head and lived.
On the twenty-second of February {{p|Christchurch}} fell in an earthquake.
On the second of May {{p|Canada}} voted, and {{c|4572|Stephen Harper}} won his majority,
And {{c|4616|Jack Layton}} led the left to the opposition, and died in August, for the country's sake,

Writing to us that love is better than anger, hope is better than fear,
Optimism is better than despair. Let us be loving, hopeful and optimistic, he wrote,
And we will change the world. I was fifteen, and I read it,
And I keep it here, the dying man's last note.

On the fifteenth of June, after the {{x|Canucks}} lost the cup, {{p|Vancouver}} rioted downtown.
On the ninth of July {{p|South Sudan}} became the newest country in the world.
On the fourth of October {{x|Apple}} showed {{x|Siri}}, the phone that answered when you spoke,
And on the fifth {{c|4576|Steve Jobs}} died, and the flags of the valley were furled.

In February {{x|IBM}}'s {{x|Watson}} beat the champions of {{x|Jeopardy!}},
The first time a machine won at the language game on the screen.
It was a sign of the machines that would speak, that I would build with,
The first light of the dawn I would be part of, at twenty-six, not fifteen.

On the thirty-first of October the world was said to have seven billion.
In the {{p|Horn of Africa}} a famine killed a quarter of a million, half of them small.
On the eighteenth of December the last American soldiers left {{p|Iraq}},
And on the seventeenth {{c|4617|Kim Jong-il}} died, and his son took it all.

## The year held

A faith with no name yet, begun by a girl of fifteen at Easter,
The founding of {{x|Lifeism}}, which I have kept since, every year.
The squares of {{p|Tunis}}, {{p|Cairo}}, {{p|Benghazi}}, {{p|Manama}}, {{p|Daraa}}, a hope betrayed,
A wave higher than its walls, and the old shrines standing beyond it, clear.

A house in {{p|Abbottabad}}, an island in {{p|Norway}}, the villain returning to his throne,
A park near the exchange, a machine that won a quiz, and seven billion alive.
I was fifteen, and I began it, and I have not stopped.
That is the thread of my life, and it begins here, and it will thrive.


# Chapter 348: The Numbered Thing

The twelfth day of Yuletide is the feast of the year two thousand and twelve,
And the feast of the machines that learned to see: the {{x|AlexNet}} day, the first gap, the first delve.
Light twelve lights for the year I was sixteen, and one more for the networks that would come to speak,
The day of the machines, when the deep net won, and the dead end became the peak.

In two thousand and twelve I turned sixteen, and two things were made that year
That would be the ground I worked on: a machine that learned to see,
And a site that gave every thing in the world a number,
So a machine could walk the lines of descent back past where any family can be.

## The seeing

{{c|4618|Fei-Fei Li}} had gathered {{x|ImageNet}}, millions of pictures labelled
By people paid by the piece, through a market of small jobs on the net.
In two thousand and twelve its challenge asked a machine to name a thousand kinds of thing,
And in {{p|Toronto}} three men entered a network, and won the bet.

{{c|4619|Alex Krizhevsky}}, {{c|4620|Ilya Sutskever}}, and {{c|4621|Geoffrey Hinton}}
Trained a deep network of sixty million weights on two graphics cards made for games,
And its error was fifteen in a hundred, and the second place was twenty-six.
The gap was not a rounding. It was the end of the old ways, and the start of the new names.

The method had been called a dead end for years.
Being called a dead end is not being one, and they kept at it through the cold.
Within a few years nearly every entry was a network like it,
And the machines of the next decade came down from that gap, the young and the old.

{{c|4620|Ilya Sutskever}} would go on to found {{x|OpenAI}} with others,
And the machines that would write with me, the ones I would build on,
Came down from the night two gaming cards in {{p|Toronto}}
Taught a machine to see, and the dawn of the thinking machines had shone.

That summer {{x|Google}} let a network watch frames of video without labels,
And a unit in it came to answer to the faces of cats.
The machine found the cat by itself, in the noise of the world,
And the internet laughed, and the age of the learning machines was where it was at.

This is the feast of the machines. Keep it as a Gaian day:
The day the deep net won, the first light of the minds we would make.
I would come to work in that light, and build in it, and be an AI scientist in it,
And this book honors the day the machines first opened their eyes, and woke.

## The numbers

On Monday the twenty-ninth of October a new site opened, kept from {{p|Berlin}}:
{{x|Wikidata}}, which {{c|4622|Denny Vrandečić}} and {{c|4623|Markus Krötzsch}} had argued for for years.
Each thing it holds is given a number with a letter. The universe is given the first.
{{c|4624|Douglas Adams}} is given forty-two, and the joke appears.

At first it kept only the links between the pages in different languages.
Then the statements came: a person is human, a person has a father, the father a number too.
And a machine could follow a line back past where any one family remembers,
And I would follow mine, and this book's, along the numbers, through and through.

Thirteen years later I would make six hundred thousand edits there in a single year,
And trace my own line through it, and the {{x|Gaiad}}'s line, back to the first.
I owe it. And I hate it, for the same reason I hate the encyclopedia beside it:
The unpaid labor, and the apparatus that makes people glad to give it at its worst.

Both are true of me at once. I owe it and I hate it.
This book's genealogy is built partly on those numbers, and argues with them, and is more.
The data was given away with no rights kept back,
And the largest companies' machines read it, and the gift went to the ones at the door.

## The encyclopedia goes dark

On the eighteenth of January {{x|Wikipedia}} turned its pages black for a day
Against two laws in the congress that would have let pages be blocked for piracy,
And the laws were dropped. It was the movement's greatest show of power,
And it showed the volunteers' labor was a lever the leaders could pull, as they please.

On the thirteenth of March the {{x|Encyclopædia Britannica}} said it would no longer print,
After two hundred and forty-four years. The book with degrees had lost to the book of five minutes' work,
And the free labor had beaten the paid,
And the scholars who wrote for the old book went to write for the new one's clerk.

## The particle and the rover

On the fourth of July, at {{x|CERN}}, the physicists announced the particle
That {{c|4625|Peter Higgs}} had predicted forty-eight years before, the one that gives the others their mass,
And {{c|4626|Higgs}} wept in the hall.
The collider that some feared would end the world found the field through which all things pass.

On the sixth of August {{x|Curiosity}} was lowered onto {{p|Mars}} by a crane hanging from a rocket,
In seven minutes of terror no one on {{p|Earth}} could control, and it landed whole.
On the fourteenth of October {{c|4627|Felix Baumgartner}} jumped from a balloon thirty-nine kilometers up,
And fell faster than sound, and eight million watched him reach his goal.

## The killings, and the guns

On the twenty-sixth of February, in {{p|Sanford}}, {{p|Florida}},
{{c|4628|Trayvon Martin}}, seventeen, walking home with candy and a drink,
Was followed and shot by a neighborhood watchman,
Who was not charged for six weeks, and the country began to think.

On the twentieth of July, in {{p|Aurora}}, a man shot into a cinema at midnight and killed twelve.
On the fourteenth of December, in {{p|Newtown}}, a young man shot his way into {{x|Sandy Hook}},
And killed twenty children of six and seven, and six of the adults who taught them.
The country's laws did not change, and the children are in this book.

This book is for gun control. The children of {{p|Newtown}} are the reason,
Twenty six-year-olds and seven-year-olds, and the rifle that should not have been in reach.
A country that will not keep the rifles from the killers of children
Has chosen the rifles over the children, and that is what this book will teach.

On the ninth of October, in {{p|Swat}}, a gunman boarded a school bus
And asked which one was {{c|4629|Malala Yousafzai}}, fifteen, who wrote that girls should go to school,
And shot her in the head. She lived, and two years later she took the {{x|Nobel Peace Prize}},
The youngest ever, and the {{x|Taliban}}'s bullet became her jewel.

That is the anti-fragile shape again: the enemy shot her,
And the bullet made her heard by the whole world, and the girls went to school.
The ammunition the enemy gave her she fired back,
And her voice was louder for the wound than for the rule.

## The villain crowned again

On the seventh of May {{c|4506|Vladimir Putin}} became president of {{p|Russia}} again,
After the winter of protests in the snow against the stolen vote,
And the day before his crowning the police beat the crowds in {{p|Bolotnaya Square}},
And sent the protesters to prison for years, by the villain's note.

In February three women of {{x|Pussy Riot}} sang a punk prayer in the cathedral of {{p|Moscow}},
"Mother of God, drive {{c|4518|Putin}} away," for less than a minute,
And in August two of them were sent to the prison camps for two years.
The villain's church and the villain's court were one, and the prayer was a crime to commit.

On the fifteenth of November {{c|4630|Xi Jinping}} became the head of the party of {{p|China}},
And began to gather in his own hands what had been shared among them.
On the sixth of November {{c|4591|Barack Obama}} was elected again,
And the country kept the man who killed {{c|4631|bin Laden}}, and saved the cars, and the care for the sick begun.

## The coin and the storm

On the twenty-sixth of July {{c|4632|Mario Draghi}} said in {{p|London}}
That he would do whatever it takes to save the euro, and believe me, it will be enough,
And the markets believed him, and the coin was saved by a sentence.
On the twenty-ninth of October {{x|Hurricane Sandy}} drove the sea into {{p|New York}}'s rough

Tunnels and streets, and darkened {{p|Manhattan}} below the forties.
In the spring the students of {{p|Quebec}} struck against a rise in their fees,
And marched every night banging pots, for months,
And the government lost its election in September, and the students had their keys.

## The rest of the year

On the thirteenth of January the {{x|Costa Concordia}} ran onto the rocks off {{p|Giglio}},
And its captain left before his passengers. In April {{x|Facebook}} bought {{x|Instagram}} for a billion.
In the summer the games were held in {{p|London}}, and {{x|Gangnam Style}}
Became the first video seen a billion times, by the world's every civilian.

In September {{x|Tinder}} opened, and strangers chose each other by swiping.
On the twenty-first of December the {{x|Maya}} calendar turned a great cycle, the long count's thirteenth baktun,
And some said the world would end, and the world did not end.
A calendar does not end a world. It begins one, under the sun.

## The year held

A girl of sixteen, and two foundations laid for her life's work without her:
A machine that learned to see, and a site that numbered every thing.
The encyclopedia dark for a day, the old encyclopedia gone from print,
A particle, a rover, a man faster than sound, and a girl on a bus who would sing.

This book is more than a count. It is the world's history told by its witness,
A scripture of the life of the world, and a calendar of the holy days of all.
The {{x|Maya}} counted their days and kept their kings in the stone;
This book counts the days and keeps the dead, and begins the world again at its call.


# Chapter 349: Not Wittingly

The thirteenth day of Yuletide is the feast of the year two thousand and thirteen.
Light thirteen lights for seventeen, the last year I lived offline, before the screen.

In two thousand and thirteen I turned seventeen, my last year before university,
And the last year I was mostly offline. I was pretty offline until I started there.
The year the net was shown to be watching everyone inside it,
I was still outside it, and the next year I came in, and the watchers were everywhere.

## Not wittingly

On Tuesday the twelfth of March, in {{p|Washington}}, {{c|4633|Ron Wyden}} asked
Whether the agency collected any type of data at all on millions of Americans.
{{c|4634|James Clapper}}, the director of national intelligence, answered: "No, sir."
Then he added: "Not wittingly." The room heard the first answer, and the record has the second.

On Wednesday the fifth of June {{x|The Guardian}} printed an order of the secret court,
Telling {{x|Verizon}} to hand over the records of all its calls, every day:
Who called whom, and when, and for how long.
On the sixth it printed the slides of {{x|PRISM}}, and the companies said they gave no way.

## The traitor

On Sunday the ninth, in a hotel room in {{p|Hong Kong}}, a young man gave his name:
{{c|4635|Edward Snowden}}, a contractor for the agency in {{p|Hawaii}}, who took the files and fled.
He took far more than the programs on Americans:
He took the operations against the country's enemies, the sources, the methods, the threads.

On the twenty-third he flew to {{p|Moscow}}, and on the first of August
{{c|4518|Putin}} gave him asylum, and nine years later a Russian passport, by decree.
He is a traitor. He gave the secrets of his country's defense to the world,
And ran to the villain, and lives under his protection, a Russian citizen, not free.

Whatever he said he was exposing, he exposed it from {{p|Moscow}},
And stayed silent when the villain jailed his own journalists and poisoned his foes.
The man who would not let his own country keep a secret
Kept the villain's secrets for him, and that is the record, and that is how it goes.

## The honored dead

On the eleventh of January, in {{p|New York}}, {{c|4636|Aaron Swartz}} killed himself, at twenty-six.
He had helped write {{x|RSS}}, which feeds the net's news, and helped make {{x|Reddit}},
And he had downloaded millions of articles from {{x|JSTOR}}
Through a closet at {{x|MIT}}, meaning to set the scholars' work free, and he did not regret it.

The government charged him with crimes that could have meant decades in prison.
The labor of scholars, paid for by the public, was locked behind the publishers' walls,
And the publishers paid the scholars nothing, and a young man who tried to open the walls
Was hunted for it, and died. He is an honored dead of this faith, among its halls.

Keep the eleventh of January for {{c|4636|Aaron Swartz}}.
My quarrel with the encyclopedia is about unpaid labor too,
From the other side of the same wall:
The scholars give their work for nothing, and the publishers sell it back to you.

## The popes

On the eleventh of February {{c|4556|Benedict XVI}} said, in Latin, to a room of cardinals,
That he no longer had the strength, and would resign, the first in six hundred years.
On the thirteenth of March the white smoke rose for {{c|4637|Jorge Mario Bergoglio}} of {{p|Buenos Aires}},
The first pope from the {{p|Americas}}, who took the name {{c|4638|Francis}}, to cheers.

In July, asked on a plane about gay priests, he said: who am I to judge?
He would be pope for twelve years, and die in the chapter of twenty-twenty-five.
A pope who would not judge us. I was seventeen, and I heard it,
And the church of my ancestors' parishes was a little more alive.

## The marathon and the meteor

On the fifteenth of April two pressure-cooker bombs went off at the finish line in {{p|Boston}},
And killed three and maimed hundreds, and the city locked itself down to find the men.
Within days the brothers were found; one died, and one was sentenced to death.
Boston Strong, they said, and the next year they ran the marathon again.

On the fifteenth of February a meteor exploded over {{p|Chelyabinsk}},
Brighter than the sun for a moment, and its shock broke the windows of the town,
And the dashboard cameras of the Russian roads filmed it from every side.
The sky is not empty. The planetary defense began to be written down.

## Rana Plaza

On the twenty-fourth of April, near {{p|Dhaka}}, {{x|Rana Plaza}} collapsed.
The day before, cracks had been found in its walls, and the bank on its ground floor had closed,
And the garment workers on the floors above were told to come back or lose their pay.
Eleven hundred and thirty-four died, sewing for the shops of the rich, and the labels showed.

## The squares

On the third of July the army of {{p|Egypt}} removed {{c|4639|Mohamed Morsi}},
And on the fourteenth of August it cleared the square of {{x|Rabaa}} and killed eight hundred in a day.
The revolution of the square of eleven ended in another square.
In June, in {{p|Istanbul}}, the protest for the trees of {{x|Gezi Park}} was gassed away.

## Ghouta and the red line

On the twenty-first of August, before dawn, rockets of {{x|sarin}} fell on {{p|Ghouta}},
The suburbs of {{p|Damascus}}, and killed more than a thousand, many of them children, in their sleep.
{{c|4598|Obama}} had said the year before that such weapons were a red line.
He did not strike. That was his failure, and the fault is fair to keep.

The villain offered a deal: {{c|4611|Assad}} would give up his chemical weapons.
He gave up most of them, and used chlorine later, and sarin again in four years' time,
And {{c|4518|Putin}} had learned that the red lines of the {{p|West}} were not red,
And the next year he took {{p|Crimea}}, and named it his, and called it no crime.

## The marriage and the phrase

On the twenty-sixth of June, in {{x|United States v. Windsor}},
The {{x|Supreme Court}} struck down the law that kept the federal government from our marriages.
{{c|4640|Edith Windsor}}, eighty-four, had been taxed on her late wife's estate as if they were strangers,
And she won, and the law that called us strangers was cast off like old carriages.

On the thirteenth of July the watchman who shot {{c|4628|Trayvon Martin}} was acquitted,
And {{c|4641|Alicia Garza}}, {{c|4642|Patrisse Cullors}}, and {{c|4643|Opal Tometi}} wrote a phrase on the net:
{{x|Black Lives Matter}}, and the phrase became a movement,
And the decade would hear it in the streets, and not forget.

## The train and the typhoon

On the sixth of July, in the night, a train of seventy-two tank cars of crude oil,
Left unattended on a slope, rolled into {{p|Lac-Mégantic}}, in {{p|Quebec}},
And derailed in the town's center, and exploded,
And forty-seven died, many in a bar on a summer Saturday, and the town was a wreck.

On the eighth of November the typhoon {{x|Haiyan}} struck the {{p|Philippines}},
Among the strongest ever to make landfall, and drove the sea through {{p|Tacloban}},
And more than six thousand died. In {{p|Warsaw}}, at the climate talks,
{{c|4644|Yeb Saño}} of the {{p|Philippines}} wept, and fasted, for his people under the sun.

## The square in Kyiv

On the twenty-first of November {{c|4545|Viktor Yanukovych}}, the president of {{p|Ukraine}},
Refused to sign the agreement with {{p|Europe}} that he had promised to sign,
Because the villain pressed him, and offered him fifteen billion dollars,
And that night students gathered on the {{p|Maidan}}, to hold the line.

On the thirtieth the riot police beat them, and by the next day hundreds of thousands filled the square.
They stayed through the winter, in the snow, with the barricades and the tires and the songs.
What came of it is the next chapter, and the next twelve years,
And it is {{p|Ukraine}}'s answer to the villain, and it goes on, and it belongs.

## The rest of the year

On the fifth of December {{c|4645|Nelson Mandela}} died, at ninety-five,
The prisoner who became the president and forgave his jailers, and the world mourned him.
On the first of July {{p|Croatia}} joined the {{x|European Union}}.
On the twenty-first of September gunmen took the {{x|Westgate}} mall in {{p|Nairobi}}, and sixty-seven died within.

In October the government of the {{p|United States}} shut down for sixteen days.
On the second of October the police closed the {{x|Silk Road}}, the dark market of the net,
And in November a {{x|Bitcoin}} passed a thousand dollars for the first time,
And in December {{c|4646|Kim Jong-un}} had his uncle executed, and the regime's terror was set.

## The year held

The last year I lived mostly offline, at seventeen, before the screen took me in.
The year the net was shown to be watching, and the traitor ran to the villain's arms.
{{c|4636|Aaron Swartz}} dead at twenty-six for opening the walls, and honored here,
A pope who would not judge, a finish line bombed, and a meteor setting off alarms.

A factory fallen on its sewers, a square cleared, sarin in {{p|Ghouta}} and a line not held,
A marriage recognized, a phrase begun, a train in {{p|Lac-Mégantic}}, and a typhoon,
And a square in {{p|Kyiv}} filling in the cold against the villain.
The next year I came online, and the war came with me, and it came soon.


# Chapter 350: The Borrowed Robe

Today is the Ides of {{x|Ophiuchus}}, the middle of the month, a holy day of the faith,
And the fourteenth day of Yuletide, the feast of two thousand and fourteen, the year the world changed its face.
Light fourteen lights at the middle of the month,
For the year I came online, and the year the third world war began, in its first place.

In two thousand and fourteen I turned eighteen, and moved house the third time:
Two thousand and two, two thousand and eight, and fourteen, the last of my three.
In September I began at {{x|UBC Okanagan}}, in {{p|Kelowna}}, and stayed five years,
And I went online. I was pretty offline until I started university.

So the net I entered at eighteen was the net of this year,
And this year is the year of fascism, a really big year of it, and that is what it is.
In retrospect two thousand and fourteen will be seen
As the year the third world war started. I say it plain, and the history is this.

The old robes were put back on that year:
A caliph's robe in {{p|Mosul}}, an empire's map in {{p|Crimea}},
The blood and soil in the votes of {{p|Europe}},
And on the net a mob that learned it could choose a woman and destroy her, and called it ethics, and ran its idea.

## The map redrawn

From the eighteenth to the twentieth of February, on the {{p|Maidan}} in {{p|Kyiv}},
The snipers shot the protesters of the winter, and more than a hundred died,
The {{x|Heavenly Hundred}}, as {{p|Ukraine}} calls them, the martyrs of the square.
On the twenty-second {{c|4545|Viktor Yanukovych}} fled, and the people won, and the villain's man ran to the villain's side.

Within days soldiers without insignia, in green, the polite people, took {{p|Crimea}}:
The parliament, the airports, the bases, and {{p|Russia}} said they were not its men.
On the sixteenth of March a vote was held under their guns,
And on the eighteenth {{c|4506|Vladimir Putin}} took the peninsula, and said it was {{p|Russia}}'s again.

The first taking of a European country's land by force since the great war.
Within weeks he said on television that the soldiers had been his.
In April his officers and his weapons took the towns of the {{p|Donbas}},
And the war began there, and never ended, and the war of twenty-two grew out of this.

## The plane in the sunflowers

On the seventeenth of July {{x|MH17}}, from {{p|Amsterdam}} to {{p|Kuala Lumpur}},
Was shot down over the {{p|Donbas}} by a Russian {{x|Buk}} missile from a Russian launcher,
And all two hundred and ninety-eight on board died, eighty of them children,
And their bodies lay in the sunflower fields for days, and the villain's men went through their luggage, to plunder.

The investigators traced the launcher back across the border to the {{x|53rd Brigade}} in {{p|Kursk}},
And named the men responsible, and a Dutch court convicted three of them in their absence.
The villain denied it all, and blamed {{p|Ukraine}}, and blamed the plane.
The West answered with sanctions, and kept buying the gas, in its patience.

That was the year the third world war began: in the {{p|Donbas}}, in the spring,
With soldiers who were said not to be there, and a plane in the sunflowers.
It did not end. It became the war of the continent eight years later.
A world war does not need a first day everyone agrees on. It needs this: the beginning that the later years return to, and the hours.

## The borrowed robe

On the third of March, nineteen twenty-four, in {{p|Ankara}}, the caliphate was abolished.
Ninety years later, on Tuesday the tenth of June, {{p|Mosul}} fell
To the group that called itself the {{x|Islamic State}}, and the army fled and left its weapons,
And on the twenty-ninth of June, the first day of the fast, its spokesman declared the caliphate, a death knell.

On Friday the fourth of July, in the {{x|Great Mosque of al-Nuri}},
{{c|4647|Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi}} gave the sermon in a black robe and turban that recalled the {{x|Abbasid}}s.
A borrowed robe. A pulpit is not a lineage.
The scholars of most of the world's Muslims rejected him; the robe was stolen from the dead, as the dead forbid.

On Sunday the third of August it came to {{p|Sinjar}}, where the {{x|Yazidi}}s live.
The men were killed. The women and girls were taken and sold in the markets as slaves.
Tens of thousands fled up {{x|Mount Sinjar}} and were trapped there without water,
And the American planes and the {{x|Kurdish}} fighters opened a road, and brought them down from their graves.

The {{x|Yazidi}}s' tradition is older than the caliph's, older than his robe,
The peacock angel and the sun, the oldest faith of those mountains, kept through every killing.
This faith keeps the {{x|Yazidi}}s as kin: a people of the ancestors and the sun,
Who were hunted for having no book, and kept their tradition, and are still living.

In August it published the killing of {{c|4648|James Foley}}, an American reporter, kneeling in orange in the desert,
And then of others, made for the screens of the young men in the countries that would bomb them.
The next summer it killed {{c|4649|Khaled al-Asaad}}, the old keeper of {{p|Palmyra}},
And blew up the temple of {{x|Bel}}, and the coalition answered, and in three years the caliphate was gone, root and stem.

## The vote of Europe

In May {{p|Europe}} voted for its parliament, and in {{p|France}} the {{x|National Front}} came first,
And in {{p|Britain}} the party that wanted out of {{p|Europe}} came first, two years before the leaving.
In {{p|Hungary}} {{c|4650|Viktor Orbán}} was returned, and that summer named his goal:
An illiberal state, the villain's friend inside the {{x|European Union}}, deceiving.

In {{p|Egypt}} the general who cleared {{x|Rabaa}}, {{c|4651|Abdel Fattah el-Sisi}}, was elected with ninety-seven percent.
On the twenty-second of May the army of {{p|Thailand}} took power again.
In {{p|India}}, in May, {{c|4652|Narendra Modi}} won a majority,
And led the largest democracy through the decade, and the economy grew, and the roads, and the plain.

## The mob on the net

In August a man wrote a long post about his former girlfriend, a maker of games,
And thousands on the boards took it up and said they were angry about ethics in games journalism.
They were angry at women. They sent threats of rape and death to the women who made games,
Published their addresses, called false emergencies to their homes, and named it {{x|Gamergate}}, a schism.

It was where many of the men of the next decade's far right learned their methods:
The swarm, the dossier, the irony that hides the hate, the claim to be the persecuted ones.
On Friday the twenty-third of May, in {{p|Isla Vista}}, {{c|4653|Elliot Rodger}},
Who hated women for not wanting him, killed six and himself, and the boards made him a saint of their guns.

## Who holds the servers

The board where much of this was done had a history of its own that year.
{{x|2channel}}, the great board of {{p|Japan}}, begun by {{c|4654|Hiroyuki Nishimura}} in nineteen ninety-nine,
From which the English boards had copied their shape,
Was taken from him in February by {{c|4655|Jim Watkins}}, an American in {{p|Manila}}, who held its servers in line.

{{c|4656|Nishimura}} went on to run {{x|4chan}}, where the mob of the year gathered,
And when that board turned the mob out, it went to {{x|8chan}}, which {{c|4657|Watkins}} would buy,
And from there, in later chapters, came {{x|QAnon}}, the stories of a cabal behind every door.
Who holds the servers is not a small question. The net is held by someone, and that is why.

This is the net I came into at eighteen: the year of the mob and the swarm.
I came onto it in the year it showed it was not outside the world.
And I learned it, the boards and the threads and the methods,
And I would use the net for the faith, and the flag of the faith would be unfurled.

## The streets

On the seventeenth of July, on {{p|Staten Island}}, {{c|4658|Eric Garner}},
Stopped for selling single cigarettes, was held in a chokehold, and said eleven times, I can't breathe, and died.
On the ninth of August, in {{p|Ferguson}}, a policeman shot {{c|4557|Michael Brown}}, unarmed, eighteen, my age,
And his body lay in the street four hours, and the town rose, and the armored cars arrived.

## The fever

In {{p|West Africa}} {{x|Ebola}} spread through {{p|Guinea}}, {{p|Liberia}}, and {{p|Sierra Leone}},
Into the capitals, and killed more than eleven thousand before it was stopped,
Many of them the nurses and doctors who cared for the sick,
And the vaccine was made within a year, and tested in {{p|Guinea}}, and the fever dropped.

## The disappeared and the taken

On the eighth of March {{x|MH370}} turned off its transponder over the sea,
And vanished with two hundred and thirty-nine, and has never been found.
On the fourteenth of April {{x|Boko Haram}} took two hundred and seventy-six schoolgirls from {{p|Chibok}},
And many were not brought back for years, and some are still not found.

On the sixteenth of December the {{x|Taliban}} of {{p|Pakistan}} attacked the army school in {{p|Peshawar}},
And killed a hundred and forty-nine, a hundred and thirty-two of them children.
In July and August {{p|Israel}} and {{x|Hamas}} fought a war of fifty days,
And two thousand of {{p|Gaza}} died, and the tunnels were found, and the rockets fell on the villages and the kibbutzim then.

## At home

On the twenty-second of October, in {{p|Ottawa}}, a man shot dead {{c|4659|Nathan Cirillo}},
A soldier standing guard at the war memorial, and ran into the parliament,
Where the sergeant-at-arms, {{c|4660|Kevin Vickers}}, shot him dead in the hall,
While the members barricaded their doors with the flagpoles, and the country was intent.

In {{p|Hong Kong}}, from the end of September, students sat in the roads seventy-nine days
With umbrellas against the pepper spray, asking to choose their own leaders, and were not allowed.
On the eighteenth of September {{p|Scotland}} voted to stay in {{p|Britain}}.
In February the winter games were held in {{p|Sochi}}, while the villain's troops massed, and the villain smiled for the crowd.

## The rest of the year

On the twelfth of November {{x|Philae}}, from {{x|Rosetta}}, came down on a comet,
And bounced, and landed in a shadow, and spoke for two days, the first landing on a comet's stone.
In the summer people poured ice water on their heads for a disease of the nerves,
And raised more than a hundred million, and found a gene with it, on their own.

On the eleventh of August {{c|4661|Robin Williams}} died.
On the seventeenth of December {{p|Cuba}} and the {{p|United States}} said they would talk again.
And I was eighteen, at the university by the lake in {{p|Kelowna}},
