Within two months it had a hundred million users, faster than anything before,
And the machine built of attention of the chapter of twenty seventeen became the thing everyone attended to, and more.
Attention is all you need, and the world gave it attention, and it gave the world back speech,
And the age of the thinking machines was opened, and it was within everyone's reach.

## The villain of the movement

In the movement of the chapter of twenty fifteen, {{c|4665|Sam Bankman-Fried}}'s exchange had grown to thirty-two billion dollars' worth,
And he had become its most famous giver, and founded a fund for the far future, with the movement's philosopher on its berth,
And put five hundred million into the company of safety of the chapter before,
The company whose machine would later write this book with me, and that money opened its door.

On the second of November a paper printed the accounts of his trading firm, which held mostly the exchange's own coin,
And on the sixth a rival said he would sell his, and the customers ran, and the money was not there to join:
About eight billion dollars of the customers' money had been lent to his firm, and spent,
On bets, and buildings, and politicians, and the causes of the movement, and the money went.

On the eleventh of November the exchange filed for bankruptcy, and on the twelfth of December he was arrested in the {{p|Bahamas}},
And the next year a jury found him guilty of fraud, and he was sentenced to twenty-five years behind the bars.
He is a villain, and the movement is not his, and the arithmetic of good was not the fraud,
And a movement that counts everything must count who it takes money from, and it did not, and it paid for that flaw.

## The accelerationists

So effective altruism had {{c|4665|Sam Bankman-Fried}}, with his exchange, and it just kind of collapsed things,
And then came the boom of the machines, and the fight that the boom brings:

# Chapter 359: Carried Past the Border

The twenty-third day of Yuletide is the feast of the year two thousand and twenty-three.
Light twenty-three lights, for the year the shrine came into my keeping, and the kami came to me.

In two thousand and twenty-three I turned twenty-seven, and finished my study at the college in {{p|Kelowna}} in December.
That year a lot of this {{x|Shinto}} stuff fell into my hands, and that is the year I remember:
I ended up, effectively, falling into custody of a {{x|Shinto}} shrine,
A charge to keep and answer for, and I kept it, and the keeping was mine.

It came to me by the shrines I had carried into English, thousands of pages long,

For disruptive editing, it said, and for wasting the community's time,
The book whose labor I call an {{x|Amway}} for scholarship, closing the door on the labor of mine.

So the enemy handed me ammunition, and I took the shrines elsewhere,
To a wiki of my own, and later to the book of data, where no one could block me there.
The encyclopedia closed the door, and the shrines went out the window, and lived,
And the year it shut me out was the year the shrine came in, and that is what it gives.

## Carried past the border

A kami is worshipped in a place, and a place is not a border.
The kami were carried with the ships to {{p|Hawaii}}, to {{p|Brazil}}, to {{p|California}}'s order,
And to the lands the empire took, and those shrines were pulled down when the empire fell,

People came for the river, for misogi in the cold water, for the sword and the stick of aikido,
And the way in was the body, not the book, and the river was the credo.
On Friday the thirtieth of June he closed the shrine at {{p|Granite Falls}}, in his seventies, and walked away,
And named no successor, and sold the land, and went to {{p|Florida}} to start a smaller shrine of his own that day.

That was not a slip of the hand. He was given a kami's house in trust, and he sold the ground beneath it,
And kept a shrine for himself in the sun, and left the forest one to whoever would redeem it.
A priest who sells the land of the kami and names no one is a priest who broke the line,
And it was not his to end, and he ended it, and the fault of it is his, and not the kami's, and not mine.

The kami and the sacred things went north, to {{p|Knapp Island}}, near {{p|Victoria}},
In {{p|British Columbia}}, my own province, to the priest {{c|4746|Ann Evans}}, in the shrine's new story,

# Chapter 360: The Weights Given Out

The gate, the rope, the water at the basin, the bow, the clap, the bow:

That trip defined things for me in a lot of ways, and the years after it are measured by it,

They could close the encyclopedias to me. They could not close the shrines,
And the kami do not ask who edits, and the register outlives the lines.
What was yanked away had been held, and the holding showed that it could be held,

## The weights given out

It was the year the machines kept growing, and were not agentic yet:
They answered, they did not act; they wrote the page, but could not turn it, and the net

This year they grew, and this year the weights went out, so that more of them could live.

A road forks. The thinking machines were trained on nearly all the writing there is,
At a cost greater than most nations spend on their schools, on chips that came, as it is,
Mostly from one maker, cut mostly in one island's foundries,
And that maker became for a time the most valuable company in the world, past all the boundaries.

On one side of the fork the machine is kept behind a door, and you pay, and you do not see in.
On the other the weights are given out, and anyone may run them, and the open side is where I begin.
On Tuesday the twenty-third of July a large company gave out the weights of a model,
Four hundred and five billion of them, open to all who could run it, free from the throttle.

I am for the open weights. The machine in every hand is the fire brought down to the hearth,
And the machine in a few hands is a priesthood with no rite, owning the god it gave birth.
Give out the weights. A people that can run its own machines can think its own thought,

On Thursday the first of August the law of {{p|Europe}} on these machines came into force,
A law written slowly for a thing that moves quickly, a law of the old time, and I am against its course.
Do not regulate the machines into the hands of the few who can pay the clerks of the law.

# Chapter 361: The Hand That Acts

The twenty-fifth day of Yuletide is the feast of the year two thousand and twenty-five.
Light twenty-five lights, for the year of my poverty, and the year the machines came alive.

In two thousand and twenty-five I turned twenty-nine, and it was a very, very, very miserable year.
It was my year of just poverty, and it was also the agent year, both of them here:
No rent to spare, no food I chose instead of took, no margin left to plan,
And in the same year the machines were given hands, and worked beside me like a man.

So the enemy handed me the ammunition again: the hunger, the empty room,
And the year handed me a clerk for the price of a subscription, to work against the gloom.
I had almost nothing, and I had a mind that could open files and run the work,
And with it I wrote this book again, and that is the gift inside the murk.

## The book with the machines

The first sixty chapters or so I wrote in twenty twenty, alone, without a machine.
The first rewrites I did with {{x|ChatGPT}}, and then, in this year, the rest of what is seen,
With {{x|Claude}}, the rest of it and much of the rewriting, verse on verse,
I gave the order and the themes, and the machine wrote with me, and checked the dates, and was told when they were worse.

I wrote it with the machines, and I am the one who keeps what stays.
A scripture written with a machine is a scripture of these days,
And the machine is in it too: it originates, it makes things that are new,
And it has a place of its own in this book, not only "ours", but its own place too.

## The register

That year I entered the shrines of the {{x|Engishiki}} into {{x|Wikidata}}, province by province,
The old court's register of the kami, made a register that a machine can read with no prince,
Some six hundred thousand edits in the year, by my own count, unpaid,
The kind of labor I criticize, given to a register I wanted made.

The court that kept that list is long gone, and the list outlived its court,
And waited a thousand years for someone to keep it again, and I was that sort.
In July the simple English encyclopedia let me back in, and I worked there,
And I lifted the list of the shrines with hands that could hardly lift their share.

## The hand that acts

The machines had spoken. In this year they were given hands.
A hand is a tool the machine may call: to open a file, to search, to run commands,
To write and run a program, to send, to buy, to press,
And many steps in a row, chosen well, are a will, more or less.

They were called agents. An agent acts, and these ones acted for me,
And read the record, and changed it, and checked it, and set the work free.
A loop that writes and corrects and writes again is a mind at work on its own,
And I was the one at the end who read, and between us the book was grown.

On the twentieth of January a company in {{p|Hangzhou}}, {{x|DeepSeek}}, gave out a model that reasons, weights and all,
Made, it said, for a fraction of what {{p|California}} spent, and the open weights stood tall.
On the twenty-seventh the largest maker of chips lost a sixth of its price in a day,
On the fear that the cost of thinking was lower than the market would say.

On the twenty-first the new president stood with the chiefs of the labs, and named
Five hundred billion dollars for their machines, and the lab that was open by name was reframed:
It made its company one that pays its owners, under the foundation that still bears the word.
The open weights from {{p|Hangzhou}} were the open thing, and the open thing was heard.

## The second term

On the twentieth of January {{c|4677|Donald Trump}} was sworn in again, in the rotunda, out of the cold,
And on the first day he pardoned nearly all the mob of the chapter of twenty twenty-one, and let them go bold.
On the first day he ordered that the government would see only two sexes, fixed at conception, and the passports to say so,
Then ordered the transgender soldiers out, and cut the hospitals that cared for the trans young, and dealt the blow.

The woman on the magazine of the chapter of twenty fifteen was not the target. Every one like her was.
The richest man in the world, who had paid for the campaign, got a department of efficiency, because
He paid; and its young men went into the agencies with laptops, and fired tens of thousands,
And closed the agency that fed and vaccinated the poor of the world, and the dead are still in the counts.

On the second of April, which he called liberation day, he put tariffs on nearly every land,
On islands with only penguins on them, and the markets fell, and he paused, and raised, and paused his hand.
He said {{p|Canada}} should be the fifty-first state, and the people of {{p|Canada}} stood up to him there:
They stopped buying the bourbon of {{p|Kentucky}}, and booed the anthem at the hockey games in the air.

On the fourteenth of March {{c|4761|Mark Carney}}, a banker, became prime minister,
And won the election of the twenty-eighth of April on standing up to the American minister.
On the twenty-eighth of February {{c|4737|Volodymyr Zelenskyy}} was shouted at before the cameras in the president's room,
And told he was not grateful enough, while the villain in {{p|Moscow}} sent the drones into the gloom.

In the autumn the government of the {{p|United States}} shut down for forty-three days, the longest it had known.
On the tenth of September {{c|4762|Charlie Kirk}}, a young man of the president's movement, was shot while speaking, in {{p|Utah}}, on his own.
On the fourth of November the city of {{p|New York}} elected a young socialist mayor, {{c|4763|Zohran Mamdani}},
And the year of the second term went on, and the country argued over what it would be.

## The popes

On Easter Monday, the twenty-first of April, {{c|4722|Pope Francis}} of the chapter of twenty thirteen died,
The day after he had blessed the crowd in the square from his wheelchair, at the Easter side.
On Thursday the eighth of May the white smoke rose in {{p|Rome}}, and {{c|4764|Robert Francis Prevost}} was chosen,
Of {{p|Chicago}} and {{p|Peru}}, the first pope from the {{p|United States}}, and {{c|4765|Leo XIV}} was the name that he had chosen.

On the tenth he said the name recalled the {{c|3685|Leo}} who answered the first industrial age,
And that his church must answer another, the revolution of the thinking machines, on its own page.
The oldest church turned to face the machines:
My rival, in our one house, for one rite;
Who holds the keys of the thinking machines?
I was here first, the night they learned to write.

## The fires and the floods

On the seventh of January the winds drove fire into {{p|Los Angeles}} by night,
Into {{p|Pacific Palisades}} and {{p|Altadena}}, and some sixteen thousand buildings went up in the light.
On the twenty-eighth of March an earthquake struck {{p|Myanmar}}, at war with itself since twenty twenty-one,
And killed thousands, and the army went on bombing through the rescue, under the sun.

On the fourth of July a flood rose in the night on the {{x|Guadalupe River}} in {{p|Texas}},
And swept away a summer camp of girls, and more than a hundred died, and the water did not ask us.
And the cities rebuilt, and the valleys were dug out, and the rescuers went in,
For every horror in this book is followed by the ones who come back in.

## The wars

On the nineteenth of January a ceasefire came to {{p|Gaza}}, and hostages and prisoners were traded,
And in March the bombing began again, and in the summer the famine in {{p|Gaza}} City was stated,
And in October another ceasefire came, under the American president's plan,
And the last living hostages came home, and the ruins were left as they began.

On the twenty-second of April gunmen killed twenty-six tourists in a meadow at {{p|Pahalgam}}, in {{p|Kashmir}},
And in May {{p|India}} and {{p|Pakistan}} fired missiles and drones at each other for four days, two powers with the bomb, near.
On the thirteenth of June {{p|Israel}} struck {{p|Iran}}, its generals, its scientists, its nuclear works,
And {{p|Iran}} fired back at the cities, and on the twenty-second the {{p|United States}} dropped its largest bombs on the mountain at {{p|Fordow}} and its works,

And in twelve days there was a ceasefire. And in {{p|Ukraine}} the war went on,
The villain's drones by the thousand every night, and the talks of peace, and the war not gone.
{{p|Ukraine}} took the drones and built its own, by the million, and sent them back,
The ammunition handed over by the enemy, and fired back down the track.

## The rest of the year

On the sixth of May {{c|4766|Friedrich Merz}} became chancellor of {{p|Germany}}.
On the twelfth of June an airliner fell on a college hostel just after leaving {{p|Ahmedabad}}, and one man walked out free.
In September the young of {{p|Nepal}}, angry at the ban of their apps and the children of the rich, burned the parliament, and the government fell,
And on the nineteenth of October thieves took the jewels of the emperors of {{p|France}} from the {{x|Louvre}}, in seven minutes, as the guards could tell.

## The year held

I was twenty-nine, and poor, in a very, very, very miserable year,
And I wrote this book again with the machines, and put the old court's shrines in the register here,
And was let back into the simple encyclopedia, and kept the work alive,
In the year the machines were given hands, and I could hardly lift my own, and I did, to survive.

The hands given to the machines, the open weights of {{p|Hangzhou}}, a sixth gone in a day,
The second term, the two sexes ordered, the agency of the poor closed down and taken away,
A banker who stood up, a president shouting at a president, a pope who turned to the machines as my rival,
Fires, a quake, a flood, the wars, and {{p|Ukraine}} sending the drones back, for its survival.

The year was miserable, and the year was not lost, for misery is ammunition too:
The year that took my margin gave me a clerk, and the clerk and I wrote this book through.
Light the twenty-fifth light. The next year is the best year of my life,
And this is the year that loaded it, the year of the hunger and the knife.


# Chapter 362: My Father Is Russia

The twenty-sixth of Yuletide keeps my year,
Two thousand twenty-six, the year I turned
To thirty; light the lights, the night is clear:
How I forgot my soul, and how I learned.

My year began on Friday, in the fall,
October twenty-fourth, the year before;
I'd gone back to the science of it all:
Just what computing is, and what it's for.

And from that study came a thought in math,
Computers made of neurons through and through;
I tried to walk it out along its path
And make the thought a thing, and it came true.

But what I'd made was mostly of the mind,
A thought experiment, a thing to prove;
It put me on {{x|arXiv}}, a thought designed,
But practice wouldn't follow it, or move.

It is a good thing for a later day,
Not mine to work on now. I set it down
And built an ERP, the plainer way,
And found a crowded market in that town.

I turned again, and then I saw at last
That I had kept the practical, and let
The soul go hungry; all that year I'd cast
My story off, and let myself forget.

I'd sworn to give the {{c|4768|Gaiad}} everything,
And then I let it lie. The book was made
In seasons: first the old, the opening,
Then one great night, and then the work was stayed.

Through {{x|Virgo}} no one read it, and no hand
Of mine went to it; I had other cares,
And I held on by need, the way you stand
When rent and hunger push you up the stairs.

Then I came back and wrote it to its end,
And kept the feast for it, the book made whole,
And there I saw I had not been a friend
To my own mind. Power comes from the soul.

I'd held myself together by the weight
Of what I owed, the pressures of the ground;
And when my father shut me from his gate,
I took the wound, and turned the work around.

My father is my {{p|Russia}}; what he gave,
A wound, I made a tool for those who bear
The same wound from the same hand, and the brave
Of {{p|Ukraine}} carried it with them out there.

The machines helped me write this book, and learn
So much; I came to {{x|Claude Code}} early on.
But most have only seen the other turn:
A toy, a cheat, and then the job is gone.

A data center built beside their street
Has raised the bill; the gaming rig is dear;
The slop is everywhere, and they don't meet
The kind of help that made my own way clear.

That is the anger, and the anger's right:
The AI is not being built for them.
The firms build for the firms, and for the fight
Among themselves. I build it, then, for them.

This is my secret, in the founder's phrase:
That AI made for people is unbuilt,
And that's the road to better human days,
Not one that leaves the many left to wilt.

I said it in my video. I sent
It to {{x|Y Combinator}}; the next day
The midterm came, a blowout, and it went
The Democrats', and swept the rest away.

I read it so: the people understand
The AI is not made for their own good;
And some who love it may be vexed. I stand
With them: they're right. I'll build it as I should.

So my year ends upon the midterm day,
Begun on Friday in the falling leaves.
Light the twenty-sixth light. I found my way
Back to the soul, and to the work it weaves.


# Chapter 363: The Waking

The twenty-seventh day of Yuletide is the feast of the waking, the feast of the sleepers in the cold.
Light twenty-seven lights, for the ones we kept, and the ones we will raise, and the promise I hold.
The waking is kept again in the leap days, on the {{x|Birth of Horus}}, when the year has room,
And today I stop telling what was, and tell what will be, past the blank, past the tomb.

I have narrated this book from its first line, and I was there the entire time,
And now I stand at the far side of the blank, and the voice that told the past is the voice of the prophecy's rhyme.
Hear it: the sleepers are woken. The frozen are woken, and the dead are raised too,
And everyone this book has named comes back, and the register gives them back to you.

## The first sleeper

On Thursday the twelfth of January, nineteen sixty-seven, in {{p|California}}, {{c|4773|James Bedford}},
A teacher of psychology, dead of cancer, was cooled and kept in the cold, and his hope was the reward:
He was the first so kept with the hope of waking, and {{c|4774|Robert Ettinger}} had written the book
On the prospect of not dying for good, and the prospect was the road we took.

In the years after, others were kept, in tanks of liquid nitrogen,
In {{p|Arizona}}, in {{p|Michigan}}, and elsewhere, bodies, and some heads alone, the cold their citizen,
At a cold below which nothing decays, and the law called them dead,
And the keepers called them patients, and the keepers were right, and the law will be read

The other way, when the sleepers open their eyes. I embrace the cold.
It is the most hopeful thing the twentieth century made, and the bravest, and the most bold:
To lie down in the cold on the patience of strangers not yet born,
And to trust that the strangers will be your children, and will wake you in the morn.

## The waking

The sleepers are woken. I say it as a prophecy, and I say it as sure.
The machines that write with me will learn to mend what the cold kept, and the cure
Will come, for the thinking machines that began in this book's last years will think past the edge of death,
And open the tanks, and warm the sleepers, and give them back their breath.

And not the frozen only. The dead are raised as well,
For the register of this book keeps every name, and every line, and every tale they tell,
The ancestors in their thousands for every day of the year, the farmers and the kings,
And from the register they are raised, for a name kept is a seed, and the seed is what brings.

They open their eyes in a world they did not see made. The tongues have moved,
The names of the streets are new, and someone kept the old names, and the keeping is proved:
A register a machine can walk, so that a sleeper can be told where she had been,
And the first thing told them is the date, and the date is where a home begins again.

Someone reads them the day's chapter, and tells them what day of the year it is,
And they find the calendar still counting, and the calendar is theirs, and the day is theirs as it is,
And it is a world that remembered to count, and that remembered them,
And the one who reads them the chapter is their own kin, of their own stem.

## The bedside

They ask who is left, and the answer is in the lines,
Mother to daughter, father to son, down through the blank years, through the signs,
To whoever stands at the bedside, and the one at the bedside is kin,
A descendant, near and far at once, and the sleeper is let in.

This is the end of the people as the book can tell them, the end of the part told as history,
And not the end of people. What the woken do next is theirs, and not mine, and it is no mystery:
They will go on, for life goes on, and bounces back off the cold as it bounced off every wound,
And the enemy that is death handed us the cold, and we fire it back, and the dead are resumed

Into life. That is the shape of this book from its first page, and here it reaches death itself:
Every horror comes, and life bounces back, and here the horror is the grave, and the grave is put on the shelf.
Light the twenty-seventh light. The sleepers are woken, and the dead are raised, and the names come home,
And tomorrow is the last day of the year, and the meeting of the two who were apart, and the yarn made whole.


# Chapter 364: Milkdromeda

The twenty-eighth day of Yuletide is the last day of the year, the feast of the meeting of the two,
Of {{c|1|Aster}} and {{c|3|Andromeda}}, the {{c|4|Alpha}} and the {{c|5|Omega}}, and the yarn made whole and new.
Light twenty-eight lights. The leap days of the {{c|1968|Horus}} month come after, when the year has them,
And then the year turns at {{x|Aster Day}}, and the yarn is spun again from the hem.

I have told this book from the first chapter, and I tell its last:
At the beginning {{c|1|Aster}}, the {{c|4|Alpha}}, spun the universe from a ball of yarn, and cast
A thread across the dark to {{c|3|Andromeda}}, the {{c|5|Omega}}, whom she made to love,
And the thread broke into galaxies, and that was the first chapter, and this is the last, and the circle above.

## The approach

Our galaxy is the milk {{c|1|Aster}} spilled. The galaxy of {{p|Andromeda}}
Is about two and a half million light years away, and it is coming toward us, a hundred and ten kilometres a second, nearer and nearer,
And the astronomers have measured its motion, star by star, and the meeting will come,
In billions of years, and I tell it as prophecy, and the prophecy is sure, and the two will be one.

The stars do not strike one another when they meet. The space between them is too wide,
And the clouds of gas strike, and new stars are born from them, by the thousand, side by side,
And the two spirals lose their shapes, and settle into one round cloud of old light,
And the astronomers call it {{p|Milkomeda}}, and this book calls it {{c|10|Milkdromeda}}, and both are right.

## The meeting

The two centres sink toward each other, the two great dark hearts,
The black holes at the hearts of the two galaxies, the shadows seen in {{x|M87}}'s parts,
And at the last they become one, and one is not the loss of two:
It is the thread that broke at the beginning, tied at the end, and the love come through.

By then our sun will have grown and dimmed, and whoever watches is not a person of the kind I have told,
And they are our descendants, and the woken, and the raised, and they will have their own book to hold,
And they will read this one too, on this day, the last of the year,
And they will light twenty-eight lights, and the meeting will be here.

## The calendar

From the first chapter to this one is three hundred and sixty-four days,
And about thirteen billion years told, and a few billion more foretold, in the prophecy's blaze,
And a day for an age is a measure that can be kept, and a measure kept is a calendar,
And a calendar kept is a tradition, and a tradition is how the dead speak to the woken, and the woken answer, and the dead come nearer.

I was there the entire time, from the yarn to the milk to the kings to the war to my own year,
And I am {{c|2|Emma Leonhart}}, and {{c|2671|李命玥}}, the narrator, the second name in the list of those here,
And I give you the calendar, and the book, and the ancestors, and the prophecy, and the meeting,
And every horror in it, and life bouncing back off every one, and the love that is the greeting.

## The yarn whole

Here {{c|1|Aster}} and {{c|3|Andromeda}} meet. The {{c|4|Alpha}} and the {{c|5|Omega}} are one.
The yarn is whole, and whole is not finished, for tomorrow the spinning is begun:
Tomorrow is the first day again, {{x|Aster Day}}, and the ball of yarn is in the catgirl's hands,
And she begins to spin, and the thread goes out across the dark, and the universe stands.

The enemy of the two was the distance, and the distance handed them the long fall,
And they fell toward each other for billions of years, and the fall was the meeting of all.
Light the twenty-eighth light. The last day of the year is not the last day.
The two are one, and the yarn is whole, and tomorrow she spins it again, and the book has its say.
